option_a:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: two alternative game environment art proposals, this image is ONE standalone landscape proposal.
Reference image is the attached Rhino site screenshot. Use it as the spatial layout and elevated three-quarter camera reference, not a UI template. Render a clean full-bleed landscape game concept with no Rhino interface, no text, no labels. Preserve the distinctive site geometry: the LARGE EMPTY WHITE KIDNEY-SHAPED UPPER PLATFORM in the left/central foreground, its curved sheer retaining rim with dark horizontal recesses; the existing thin dark curving road and its junction crossing behind the development; the multilayer white megastructure on the right and turquoise water below; the tiny existing triangular initial ruin on the LOWER foreground promenade remains a minor landmark. The intervention belongs ON TOP OF THE LARGE FOREGROUND PLATFORM, IN FRONT OF THE DARK ROAD, not on a distant background hill, not on the lower promenade. Keep the dark road clear and its course intact.
Landscape: turn that upper plateau into a continuous meadow with THREE broad, soft, asymmetrically arranged earth mounds of different sizes and heights, merging through shallow saddles and a legible winding walking route. Visibly readable low / middle / highest crests, gentle traversable slopes, not three steep cones, not a single uniform tilted plane, no cut terraced retaining steps. Keep breathing space around the existing road. Put ONE new circular near-future building on the highest mound. Terrain and structure must visibly belong to this actual site.
Art direction: optimistic abandoned near-future infrastructure reclaimed by nature, simple convincing futuristic construction, clean large silhouettes and selective decay. Stylized painted game environment, matte ivory composite/concrete, dark inset frames and glazing, softly painted grasses and overlapping flat-colored leaf clusters. Turquoise water, restrained pale green / warm yellow grass, a few trees. Broad readable light/shadow, warm clear daylight, game art rather than photoreal grime. Weathering at joints, roof gaps and drainage edges; climbing leaves in irregular connected patches, exposed architecture remains dominant. No classical stone temples, no ancient columns, no medieval masonry, no statues, no magical ruins, no colossal skyscrapers, no floating unsupported structure. Distant context slightly simplified so the new landforms and building are clear. Show the whole target plateau and sufficient surrounding geography to judge placement. Building occupies roughly a third of target plateau width, leaving a generous playable meadow. Landscape 16:9.
VERSION A — LOW ANNULAR OBSERVATORY. A quiet, horizontal, single-story circular research/observation pavilion: a thin broad annular roof with a large circular open-sky courtyard, an offset second thin roof rim making a precise layered silhouette, an open side entrance visible along the walking route. Dark recessed curved window bands broken by functional wall sections; a handful of slender metal supports with actual connections, not a classical colonnade. One missing curved roof sector reveals secondary metal ribs and the courtyard; intact members remain structurally supported. Inner courtyard vegetation grows through disused planters. Local grasses climb onto one low roof edge. The architecture is clearly a future public/research facility that has fallen quiet, not a pristine occupied resort. Low profile emphasizes the three mounds; longest roof line sits on the highest crest. Make a polished yet buildable concept proposal.

VERSION B — OPENED DOME PAVILION. A distinctly different compact circular, low flattened dome-shell research conservatory on the highest crest: sweeping pale curved shell segments, six broad radial structural ribs, a clear off-center oculus, dark blue-gray glazing recessed between a FEW ribs. One quadrant of the dome skin is missing, exposing supported steel substructure and giving a strong asymmetrical open silhouette. A wide curved entry cut faces the meadow path. A low circular base meets the sloping ground through a short accessible graded apron. The structure is about two stories high at its crown, emphatically wider than tall. Vegetation threads through missing glazing and one shell seam; a few small trees inside the opened quadrant, not a jungle engulfing every surface. Engineering joints, thin panel edges and dark structural reveals make it distinctly near-future. Avoid a geodesic triangle ball or a shiny spaceship. This option should feel like an identifiable distant landmark while keeping the same gentle three-mound terrain and reference-site framing as option A.
relocated_a:
Use case: precise-object-edit / stylized-concept.
Image 1 is the CLEAN EXISTING CONCEPT TO EDIT. Image 2 is the SAME concept with the user's RED ARROW AND CIRCLE, used ONLY as a relocation guide.
Move the existing single annular futuristic pavilion from its back-left position to the FRONT-CENTER HILLOCK INSIDE THE RED CIRCLE in image 2. The new building's footprint is centered approximately x=0.53, y=0.48 of the image, on the upper grassy plateau immediately behind its curved front retaining edge. It must NOT remain in the old back-left position, must NOT be duplicated, and must NOT be moved onto the lower promenade. Completely remove the old back-left building and restore that area to a broad low grassy mound with a few trees.
Preserve this exact pavilion design: low, single-story circular research/observation facility, a wide thin ivory annular roof, open central courtyard, dark recessed glazing, one missing roof sector exposing supported metal ribs, selective climbing leaf clusters at the joints. Near-future nature-reclaimed infrastructure, not ancient ruins. Keep its footprint scale broadly similar to the original, comfortably fitting the front-center mound.
Adjust the three gentle landforms coherently: the new front-center building mound is now the HIGHEST broad crest, with two lower rounded grassy hills behind/alongside it and shallow saddles between. Maintain gentle playable slopes; do not create a steep cone or an unsupported elevated plinth. Re-route the narrow paths to approach the pavilion entrance from the foreground/cave side; keep a visible planted-grass approach and small graded apron. The intention is a landmark visible when the player exits the birth cave along the lower foreground promenade: keep the pavilion's front silhouette and roof rim exposed above the plateau edge; no tall foreground trees blocking this direction. Show an inviting entrance facing toward that foreground route, not the back of the building.
INVARIANTS: same elevated three-quarter camera, same overall white megastructure/platform outlines, dark road course and bridges behind, turquoise water shapes, tiny triangular initial ruin on the lower promenade, lighting, stylized painted rendering and palette. Change only the pavilion location, local mound hierarchy and connecting paths/planting needed for that move. No additional buildings, no text, no red marks or annotations in output. Output one clean full-bleed landscape concept image.
entrance_gentle_terrain_a:
Use case: stylized-concept / precise-object-edit.
Input image: the APPROVED relocated annular pavilion concept. Use it as the exact site and architectural continuity reference. Make ONE polished landscape architectural concept image of the revised building and its terrain, closer than the reference so the birth-cave-facing facade is readable, while still showing the footprint of the three mounds and some of the front platform rim. Elevated front three-quarter view FROM THE FOREGROUND / BIRTH-CAVE SIDE looking toward the pavilion. No UI, labels, text, watermarks or panels.

CRITICAL TERRAIN REVISION from the client: physically MOVE THE LARGEST MOUND TO UNDER THE BUILDING in the FRONT-CENTER of the upper platform, where the approved relocated building now stands. The building must sit on the broad crest of that largest mound, not in a low saddle between taller hills. Shape one wide, gently domed grassy mound under the whole pavilion and approach; its top subtly higher than the other two. TWO secondary mounds behind and to the sides are noticeably LOWER and smaller, merging through shallow saddles. ALL three are LOW and SOFT, no steep conical hills, no large elevation difference, no dramatic mountain or tall retaining podium. The building roof, not the terrain, should dominate the silhouette. Its accessible approach is a gentle curved rising path over lawn, with a modest graded foundation meeting the slope naturally. The main mound base is substantially wider than the pavilion. Preserve the existing hard curved platform perimeter and dark roads behind, not new steep cliffs in the meadow.

BUILDING: preserve the approved single-story, circular, low annular pavilion with a large open central garden and thin broad matte ivory ring roof, dark inset glazing, warmer grey/brown exposed support structure. Keep its approved front-center position on the upper platform. Develop the face toward the birth-cave approach into a MEMORABLE ASYMMETRICAL NEAR-FUTURE ENTRANCE:
- A restrained parametric family of 9-12 slender curved vertical fins / structural ribs along the front ring facade. Their spacing gradually widens and their twist/depth gradually increases approaching an offset entrance, opening a legible curved funnel into the courtyard. They have clear bolted base/top connections and follow the ring geometry; fewer strong members, not a dense decorative cage, not ancient classical columns.
- One side of this facade remains mostly intact with clean ivory composite cladding and a dark window ribbon; the other side has LOST its skin and glazing across a coherent curved sector, revealing its supporting metal ribs and secondary roof lattice. A few surviving cladding panels have clean broken edges; structural members remain credibly attached. No random rubble pile, no medieval stone ruins, no Roman arches.
- The damaged facade sector continues into a missing portion of the annular roof on the approach side, connecting opening, exposed skeleton and daylight as one architectural gesture. Keep most of the roof ring readable.
- From the entrance see a glimpse of a designed courtyard reclaimed by nature: one small sculptural tree, irregular planted beds within a few simple curved planter edges, a narrow weathered walking strip and a small shallow reflective basin. The garden should tease exploration through the damaged opening. Planting clustered at joints and sheltered corners, not wrapping every surface uniformly. Keep the facade's front silhouette visible; no tall foreground tree blocking the cave-side view.
- Clearly abandoned near-future public/research building being reclaimed, with precision panel joints and restrained exposed engineering. Not a pristine hotel, not an ancient temple, not a spaceship.

STYLE: same warm sunny stylized painted game art as the reference, simple large readable silhouettes, overlapping flat-color plant clusters, matte pale walls, fresh pale-green / gold meadow, turquoise water hints. Some vines and broken cladding give coherent uneven decay; avoid photoreal noisy dirt, hyperdense leaf textures, excessive debris and overcomplicated ornament. Keep sufficient context to evaluate gentle landform hierarchy. Do not add another pavilion or duplicate the building in the old back-left location. ONE landscape concept, around 16:9.
